title: Read the platform guards by status
brief: Azure AI Content Safety and Foundry guardrails ship classifiers for harm, jailbreaks, document attacks, protected material and groundedness. Which are on by default, which are preview or retired, and where does each stop covering you?

blocks.text: What the platform gives you, with status on 2026-10-13

blocks.caption: Azure AI Content Safety and Foundry guardrail features
head: Capability
What it does and limits
Status
rows: Hate and fairness, sexual, violence, self-harm, for text and images. Foundry guardrails use four levels (safe is annotated and never filtered, then low, medium, high) with thresholds Off, Low, Medium or High [[r6]]

Hate, violence, sexual and self-harm at Medium on prompts and completions, user prompt attack on prompts, protected material text and code on completions. It covers Foundry Models sold by Azure except audio transcription, and every setting is configurable [[r2]] [[r1]]

User prompt attacks (change system rules, conversation mockup, role-play, encoding) and document attacks. The standalone API takes one `userPrompt` and up to five `documents` and returns `attackDetected`. In Foundry, user attacks are scanned at input and document attacks at input and tool response [[r3]]
GA since Aug 2024, tested on English only [[r10]]

Tags documents as lower trust by base64 encoding them. Off by default, Chat Completions only, models only. Raises token counts, and the model may mention base64. A Microsoft paper reports attack success falling from above 50% to below 2% on GPT-family models [[r12]]
Checks an answer against supplied sources, with optional correction. English-optimised and available in specific regions [[r4]]

Text filter flags known text such as lyrics, articles and recipes. Code filter flags matches to GitHub repositories, with an index current only through 2023-04-06. English only, and completions need at least 110 characters [[r5]]
Text GA since Aug 2024, code listed without a Preview label in the Foundry controls table

Standard trains a text-only model and its retirement date, 2026-09-01, has passed while the concept page still says retiring and points to Foundry custom text classification. Rapid uses an LLM for emerging incidents on text and images [[r7]]
Standard retired or retiring, rapid preview
Flags misaligned or premature tool use [[r1]]
Scans model output only for personal data, with annotate or annotate and block [[r8]]

items.label: Prompt Shields input
items.note: Prompt up to 10K characters, up to five documents with 10K characters in total.

items.label: Groundedness sources
items.note: Per call, with text plus query up to 7,500 characters (preview API).

items.label: Protected material minimum
items.note: For scanning completions, not user prompts.

blocks.title: Where to apply the controls
blocks.intro: The same classifiers can be attached at three levels. The level decides what is scanned and who owns the failure.

options.name: Model deployment guardrail
options.summary: A guardrail attached to the model deployment, with `Microsoft.DefaultV2` by default.
pros: Covers every app that calls the deployment
cons: No tool call or tool response controls
Does not follow your agent logic
options.bestWhen: Prompt-in, answer-out apps with no tools.
options.avoidWhen: Agents with tools or untrusted tool results.

options.name: Agent guardrail (Foundry Agent Service)
options.summary: A guardrail assigned to an agent, with tool call and tool response intervention points.
pros: Scans tool calls and tool responses (preview)
Hosted agents also get network egress controls (preview)
cons: It fully overrides the model's guardrail, so omissions are silent
Applies only to agents built in Foundry Agent Service
Annotate is not available for agents, only annotate and block
Preview risks such as Spotlighting and Groundedness are not yet supported for agents
options.bestWhen: Agents built in Foundry Agent Service that call tools.
options.avoidWhen: Agents run elsewhere, since registering them in the Foundry Control Plane does not apply the guardrail.

options.name: Your own calls to the Content Safety APIs
options.summary: Call Prompt Shields, protected material or groundedness from your own code.
pros: You control parallelism and fail-closed rules
cons: You own limits, retries and latency
Each API has its own character limits
options.bestWhen: Custom orchestration, non-Foundry runtimes, or checks at points the platform does not expose.
options.avoidWhen: A platform guardrail already covers the need.

blocks.title: Foundry agent with a guardrail at each intervention point
blocks.alt: A prompt from the user passes an input scan, the model proposes a tool call that passes a tool call scan, the tool response passes a document attack scan, and the draft answer passes an output scan before reaching the user.
blocks.src:
sequenceDiagram
  participant U as User
  participant G as Guardrail
  participant M as Model
  participant T as Tool
  U->>G: Prompt
  G->>M: Passes input scan
  M->>G: Proposed tool call
  G->>T: Passes tool call scan
  T->>G: Tool response
  G->>M: Passes document attack scan
  M->>G: Draft answer
  G->>U: Passes output scan
blocks.caption: Tool call and tool response scanning are preview features for agents, checked 2026-10-13.

items.symptom: A tool response carries an injected instruction and nothing flags it.
items.cause: The agent's guardrail fully overrides the model's and has no tool response control.
items.fix: Add the tool response intervention point (preview) with document attack detection, and test with a planted instruction.

items.symptom: A control added to an agent's guardrail never fires.
items.cause: Preview risks such as Spotlighting and Groundedness are not yet supported for agents, so the control does not take effect for the agent.
items.fix: Read the supported-risk list before assuming coverage, and test the agent, not the model.

items.symptom: A very long prompt is only partly moderated.
items.cause: Limits apply. The Content Safety page says Foundry guardrails moderate the first 1,000 characters for text scenarios, and its exact scope is unclear. Standalone calls cap at 10K characters.
items.fix: Test with long inputs on your own deployment, split text for standalone calls and cap input size deterministically.

items.cause: Prompt Shields, protected material and groundedness were tested on English only.
items.fix: Build per-language red-team sets and add a layer you can tune.

items.symptom: Leadership says content filters stop prompt injection.
items.cause: Prompt Shields is a probabilistic detector, not a complete defence.
items.fix: Layer prompt hardening, Spotlighting, Prompt Shields, least-privilege tools and deterministic blocking of exfiltration paths, as the MSRC defence-in-depth post describes [[r11]].

blocks.title: Say the status, and the date
blocks.md: Features move between preview, GA and retired. As of 2026-10-13, Prompt Shields is GA, groundedness, Spotlighting, task adherence, PII filtering and agent tool controls are preview, and Custom categories (standard) is past its 2026-09-01 retirement date. Name the status and the date you checked in an interview answer, and confirm in the portal before you promise a feature.

quiz.q: A web search tool returns a page with an injected instruction. The model deployment's guardrail scans documents, but the agent has a custom guardrail with only user input and output controls. Why is the injection not scanned?
options: Prompt Shields cannot scan documents at all, only user prompts
Tool responses are scanned only when the model deployment also sets a severity threshold for them
Document attack scanning is skipped for any content that was not written in English
The agent's guardrail fully overrides the model's and contains no tool response control
quiz.explain: An agent is checked against the guardrail assigned to it, not its model's, and this one has no tool response control. Prompt Shields does have a document attack shield, the model's thresholds do not carry over, and English-only testing is a separate limitation that does not explain a missing control.

quiz.q: Select every true statement about Prompt Shields.
options: It has two shields: user prompt attacks and document (indirect) attacks
The standalone API takes one `userPrompt` and up to five `documents`
It removes the need for least-privilege tool permissions
It was tested on English only, so test other languages yourself
quiz.explain: The docs describe the two shields, the call shape and the English-only testing. A probabilistic detector never replaces least privilege, which limits damage when a detection is missed.

quiz.q: Match each feature to its status as of 2026-10-13.

pairs.r: Retirement date 2026-09-01 has passed, confirm in the portal

quiz.explain: Status changes what you can promise. The custom categories page still says retiring after its date passed, which is why the portal is the source of truth.

takeaways: Prompt Shields is GA, and groundedness, Spotlighting, PII filtering and agent tool controls are preview as of 2026-10-13
An agent's guardrail replaces its model's, so tool coverage must be added explicitly
Several features were tested on English only, so build per-language tests
Content filters are one layer, not a defence against prompt injection
